title: Crosswind Cut
primary_metric: net forward-progress thrust (the total thrust vector's component along the delivery heading, after subtracting the vector needed to cancel the crosswind) per amp drawn

options.B: Bolt on Configuration Albatross — the low-KV motor and large propeller

reinforcement_note: This is a second-pass/redundancy case per the batch instructions (see _new_coverage_note below), not a fresh-gap case, which is why new_coverage[] is honestly empty rather than padded. Adjacent uncovered skills in the same domain group were checked and ruled out before accepting the zero: the Pre-Calculus/Vectors group's other unclaimed labels at authoring time (e.g. Component Form Of A Vector, Vector Addition And Scalar Multiplication By Component) do not match any deliverable this case's math actually forces -- D1-D3 exercise exactly the 7 already-claimed vector/dot-product skills (Vector, Magnitude, Unit Vector, Dot Product, and their three 'how to' pairs) and no others, and the two round-out skills (Variable, How to find the percent of a number) are forced by D4/D5 as documented in LEARNING_GOALS.md. Claiming an unforced skill just to post a non-empty new_coverage[] would be exactly the fabrication SPEC §8/T1-11 exist to prevent.

cohort_bands.note: Run all four anchors as a single whole-room discussion; the vector diagram (D2) works best sketched together on one shared board before Heroes split off to compute D3/D4 individually.

Split into 2-3 small groups for the Data Deep Dive so every Hero personally builds at least one configuration's D1-D3 chain before the room reconvenes for the Twist and Deep Conflict; cold-call across groups during the D4 comparison so no group can hide behind a groupmate's arithmetic.

deliverables.text: A thrust-and-current table for each configuration, drawn from the manufacturer performance data in Appendix A: total available thrust (summed across all motors as a vector sum) and current draw at the throttle setting used for today's route.

A crosswind-cancellation vector diagram for each configuration: the crosswind vector, the delivery-heading unit vector, and the corrective thrust vector each configuration must supply to cancel the crosswind and hold the corridor centerline, with the full vector subtraction shown for at least one configuration.

A net forward-progress thrust table for each configuration: the dot product of that configuration's total available thrust vector with the delivery-heading unit vector, after the crosswind-cancellation component from D2 has been subtracted out, reported in the same units for both configurations.

A thrust-per-amp comparison table showing, for each configuration, the manufacturer's advertised calm-air thrust-per-amp figure and the net-forward-progress-thrust-per-amp figure computed from D3 and D1, with arithmetic shown for both rows.

A battery-reserve check for each configuration: using the current draw from D1 and the reserve rule in Appendix C, the percentage of the mandatory reserve remaining in the pack at touchdown on today's route.

balance.argument_a: At the route's real 90% throttle setting, Configuration Sparrow (4 motors) delivers 11,128 g of total thrust on 82.4 A. After the crosswind-cancellation cost (D2, cos theta ~= 0.8975 from MA1/MA2/MA4) is subtracted, that is 9,987.5 g of net forward-progress thrust, or 121.21 g/A -- beating Albatross's 119.07 g/A by 1.8%. T-Motor's own throttle-sweep data shows the two combos' efficiency curves cross between roughly 70-80% throttle; below that crossover Albatross is more efficient (its 40%-throttle advertised figure, 264.9 g/A, beats Sparrow's 238.3 g/A by about 11%), but above it -- at this route's actual 90% throttle -- Sparrow has become the more current-efficient combo. The argument is that the real, sourced, throttle-matched number (121.21 vs. 119.07 g/A) is the one that governs this flight, not the lower-throttle advertised spec.
balance.argument_b: Configuration Albatross's advertised calm-air thrust-per-amp figure is 264.9 g/A versus Sparrow's 238.3 g/A -- an ~11% efficiency edge at the 40% throttle point T-Motor uses for its headline number. Even after paying the identical crosswind-cancellation cost as Sparrow (the same cos theta ~= 0.8975 factor applies to both, since MA1/MA2/MA4 are common to both configurations), Albatross still totals more raw thrust at 90% throttle (15,636 g on 117.84 A, versus Sparrow's 11,128 g on 82.4 A). The argument is that a motor/prop pairing with an 11%-higher headline efficiency figure and a larger absolute thrust reserve deserves more trust than a 1.8% margin resting on a single throttle-sweep data point -- the sourced 90% row leaves little room for measurement noise before Albatross overtakes it.
balance.margin_basis: (net forward-progress thrust per amp, better configuration - net forward-progress thrust per amp, worse configuration) / net forward-progress thrust per amp, worse configuration x 100, where net forward-progress thrust = dot product of the configuration's total thrust vector (Appendix A, D1) with the delivery-heading unit vector, after subtracting the crosswind-cancellation vector (Appendix B, Appendix D MA1/MA2, D2), and current draw is Appendix A's sourced current-draw figure at the modeled throttle setting. Computed once Appendix A's T-Motor combo data and Appendix D's crosswind-angle assumption are filled by case-research.

modeling_assumptions.basis: No public source names a wind reading for a fictional corridor; 15 mph is well below the NWS Wind Advisory threshold (sustained 31-39 mph) [S3] and below the ~27-31 mph small-UAS 'Level 6' wind-resistance industry benchmark [S4] — an ordinary, sub-advisory crosswind reading.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Common to both configurations (sets the wind-correction angle), so it does not change the ranking between the two configurations' net-forward-progress-thrust-per-amp, only its magnitude.

modeling_assumptions.assumption: Crossing angle between corridor heading and crosswind direction of travel
modeling_assumptions.basis: Chosen to make the crosswind's course-perpendicular component dominant (sin 80 deg ~= 0.985), consistent with the Background's 'close to a right angle' framing, while avoiding a contrived exact 90 deg.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Common to both configurations, so it does not change the ranking between the two configurations' net-forward-progress-thrust-per-amp, only its magnitude.

modeling_assumptions.assumption: Number of motors on Drone 114's airframe
modeling_assumptions.basis: No public airframe spec exists for the fictional Drone 114. Quadcopter is the most common multirotor layout for medium-lift regional delivery platforms in this thrust class, comparable in scale to real short-hop multirotor delivery services such as Flytrex [S6].
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Does not affect the ranking between the two configurations' per-amp comparison, because motor count scales both configurations' total thrust and total current identically, cancelling out of the per-amp ratio.

modeling_assumptions.basis: No public speed spec exists for the fictional Drone 114. Matches the DJI FlyCart 30's published maximum automatic-flight cruising speed [S5], the closest real published cruise speed for a pure multirotor (non-fixed-wing) delivery drone.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Sets the wind-correction angle identically for both configurations, so it does not flip the ranking between them. Feeds the D5 reserve-check flight time.

modeling_assumptions.basis: No public route spec exists for the fictional Swiftwing corridor. Matches Flytrex's published Sky2 delivery radius [S6], a comparable real short-hop multirotor delivery operation, and is consistent with the flight endurance the MN5008-class current draw and MA6's battery capacity actually support.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Feeds the D5 reserve check only; does not enter the D3/D4 per-amp comparison between configurations.

modeling_assumptions.basis: No public battery spec exists for the fictional Drone 114 (capacity is an airframe-level choice, not a motor spec). 22,000 mAh sits within the commonly available 16,000-24,000 mAh 6S range for this thrust class of motor [S7].
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Feeds the D5 reserve check only; does not enter the D3/D4 per-amp comparison between configurations.

modeling_assumptions.assumption: Swiftwing's mandatory battery reserve at touchdown
modeling_assumptions.basis: No public reserve rule exists for the fictional Swiftwing. Modeled on manned aviation's VFR fuel-reserve principle (14 CFR 91.151 requires 30 minutes' additional fuel at normal cruise beyond the point of intended landing for day VFR flight) [S8], adopting an analogous fixed-fraction battery-energy reserve within the 20-30% range commonly cited as small-UAS practice.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Feeds the D5 reserve check only; does not enter the D3/D4 per-amp comparison between configurations.
